question: Which patient condition makes passing a nasogastric tube through the nose absolutely unsafe?
explanation: Passing a tube through the nose in a patient with a skull fracture risks entering the intracranial vault. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T2#GNS212_U1_T2_h1)

question: Why is feeding through a nasogastric tube preferred over total parenteral nutrition when the digestive tract works?

options.A: It avoids the need for fluid balance charts
options.B: It requires less monitoring of blood glucose
options.D: It is completely free of infectious risks

explanation: Enteral feeding keeps the gut mucosa active, preventing atrophy and bacterial translocation from the bowel lumen. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T2#GNS212_U1_T2_h1)

question: What is the standard tube size range for an adult nasogastric insertion?
explanation: Adults generally require a 14 to 16 Fr tube to allow adequate flow for feeding and decompression without excessive mucosal pressure. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T2#GNS212_U1_T2_h2)

question: Checking the patency of both nostrils before NG insertion helps the nurse decide what?

options.A: If the stomach is currently empty of contents
options.B: Which side has better airflow for safe passage
options.C: Whether the patient has a swallowing reflex
options.D: How much lubricant to apply to the tube tip

explanation: Assessing airflow and patency ensures the nurse chooses the clearest nostril, reducing trauma during insertion. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T2#GNS212_U1_T2_h2)

question: What does the letter E stand for in the NEX measurement method?
explanation: NEX stands for Nose to Earlobe to Xiphoid process, which estimates the internal distance to the stomach. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T2#GNS212_U1_T2_h3)

question: A patient coughs and turns dusky blue while you are advancing an NG tube. What action should you take?

options.C: Give the patient water to drink
options.D: Listen over the chest with a stethoscope

explanation: Coughing and cyanosis indicate the tube has entered the respiratory tract instead of the esophagus. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T2#GNS212_U1_T2_h3)

question: What is considered the gold standard method for confirming nasogastric tube placement?
explanation: An abdominal X-ray gives visual proof of the exact anatomical location of the distal tube tip. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T2#GNS212_U1_T2_h4)

question: Why is listening with a stethoscope over the stomach while pushing air not recommended anymore for checking tube placement?

options.A: It exposes the patient to dangerous levels of radiation
options.B: It causes severe trauma to the gastric mucosa
options.C: It requires specialized equipment that is rarely available
options.D: Air sounds can easily be transmitted from other areas

explanation: Injecting air can be heard over the epigastrium even when the tube is misplaced in the esophagus or lungs. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T2#GNS212_U1_T2_h4)

question: What is the recommended minimum head-of-bed elevation during a nasogastric feeding?
explanation: Elevating the head of the bed to at least 30 degrees uses gravity to prevent reflux and pulmonary aspiration. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T2#GNS212_U1_T2_h5)

question: What is the primary purpose of flushing an NG tube with water before and after medication administration?

options.A: To prevent tube occlusion from drug residue
options.C: To provide total daily fluid requirements
options.D: To cool down warm liquid medications

explanation: Water flushes clear the narrow lumen of the tube, stopping medications from reacting and clogging the line. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T2#GNS212_U1_T2_h5)

question: How can a nurse prevent pressure ulcers on the nares of a patient with an NG tube?

options.A: Remove the tube every shift for resting the skin
options.B: Lubricate the outside of the nostril with heavy ointment
options.C: Apply tight gauze wrapping around the bridge of the nose
options.D: Secure the tube properly and clean the nares daily

explanation: Daily cleaning and proper securing prevent the tube from pressing too hard against delicate nasal cartilage. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T2#GNS212_U1_T2_h6)

question: A patient receiving an NG feeding develops diarrhea. What is a common contributing factor?

options.D: Tube placed in the left bronchus

explanation: Cold formula can cause gastrointestinal cramping and rapid transit, leading to diarrhea. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T2#GNS212_U1_T2_h6)

question: Why should a patient hold their breath during the removal of an NG tube?

options.A: To close the glottis and prevent aspiration
options.C: To relax the abdominal wall muscles
options.D: To prevent sudden episodes of vomiting

explanation: Holding the breath closes the airway, stopping any residual fluid in the tube from entering the trachea during extraction. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T2#GNS212_U1_T2_h7)

question: Which detail is most important to document right after successfully placing a new NG tube?

options.A: The total cost of the equipment consumed
options.B: The brand name of the feeding formula used
options.C: The external length measurement at the naris
options.D: The name of the assistant who held the light

explanation: Recording the exit mark lets future shifts quickly check if the tube has slipped inward or been pulled out. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T2#GNS212_U1_T2_h7)
